evidence.explanation: The setter wrapper implements selection validation/allocation/storage through different JS primitives. Four source-call edges describe one delegation cause; tested explicit-coordinate creation/update behavior is present. This does not prove all argument forms, invalid-input diagnostics, random-coordinate or mixed-frame behavior.
evidence.proof: Twenty four-argument targets: values0,1,2,7,126 × default and translated map origins × two interior coordinates; eight two/three-argument controls cover fresh creation and default value1. Exact C l_selection_setpoint with fixed typed stack/coordinate adapters and real selection storage functions matches all1680 bytes and bounds. Existing JS selections retain identity and an unrelated anchor point; fresh results have only the requested point.
evidence.control: Two-argument calls create a fresh selection; three-argument calls use default1 and preserve an existing anchor. Public JS level_init/map establishes valid state/frame; exported production l_selection_setpoint is invoked with that state/frame and null current room. The C adapter implements the equivalent explicit frame offset, not a full Lua VM or general coordinate resolver. Storage values fit signed char after+1. No RNG, subroom, out-of-bounds, random coordinate, relative selection representation, errors, mixed frames or runtime claims.
